dedupe_keys.name: travel times and distances to health services in australia driving time from every mesh block to the nearest hospitals emergency departments gps and pharmacies

description: This data set gives, for every small area in Australia, how far people have to drive to reach the nearest hospital, emergency department, general practitioner and pharmacy. It was produced by a research team and described in a 2025 Scientific Data paper, with the data on figshare. Using the Open Source Routing Machine on OpenStreetMap roads, the authors computed driving times and distances from the centroid of each 2021 Mesh Block, about 368,000 of them, to the nearest public and private hospitals, emergency departments, GPs, bulk-billing GPs and pharmacies, and added population counts, remoteness classes (Modified Monash Model) and population-weighted averages by postal area, Statistical Area Level 2 and state. Coverage is all of Australia. The tables are free and available to download as CSV under CC BY 4.0, together with the road extract used, and the Python code is on GitHub so the method can be re-run for other countries. Caveats: times assume normal driving conditions and the service lists of the study date, and access by public transport or air retrieval is not modelled. Simulation uses: estimating how road closures in bushfires and floods lengthen access to emergency care, targeting remote areas for service planning, and weighting exposure by access. Related records: the HeiGIT accessibility indicators (data-heigit-accessibility-indicators) and the China hospital travel time maps (data-china-1km-hospital-travel-time-accessibility).
